title: How to automate lead follow-up from Gmail | 50agents
description: Automate lead follow-up from Gmail: log each lead with a last-contact date, follow up in the same thread after N quiet days, and stop when they reply.
h1: How to automate lead follow-up from Gmail
answer: Keep a list of leads with a stage and a last-contact date, and have a tool check each morning for leads you contacted three or more days ago who have not replied, then draft a short follow-up in the same Gmail thread.
The part most setups get wrong is the stop: a reply from the lead, from a colleague of theirs or in a new thread must end the sequence.

body.p: Every follow-up tool, from a Gmail add-on to a CRM sequence, runs the same loop. Knowing it lets you judge any tool in five minutes.

sections.h2: What Gmail can do on its own

body.p: Gmail can remind you, not send for you. Its nudges suggest emails to follow up on, and you write the follow-up yourself. To send or draft follow-ups automatically, you need an add-on (GMass, Mixmax and others work inside Gmail), a CRM with sequences, or an automation tool that reads your Gmail.

Whatever you use sends from your account, so Gmail’s limits apply to it. A Google Workspace user can send up to 2,000 messages a day, 500 on a trial, and hitting the limit stops all your sending for up to 24 hours. A personal Gmail account is limited around 500 emails a day. Follow-ups to a few dozen leads are nowhere near either; a bulk sequence can be.

method.h2: How to set it up, step by step

steps.title: Make the lead list
steps.body: Name, email, company, stage (New, Contacted, Replied, Won, Lost), last contact and next follow-up. A sheet works; a CRM works; the columns are what matter.

steps.title: Decide the gap and the number of follow-ups
steps.body: Three days for warm leads, a week for cold ones, and two or three follow-ups at most. Write it down; it becomes the rule.

steps.title: Write each follow-up to move one step
steps.body: Not "just checking in". Offer the next step: a call time, a shorter version of the quote, a question that is easy to answer.

steps.title: Send in the same thread
steps.body: A reply in the original thread keeps the context for the lead and keeps your reply detection simple.

steps.title: Detect replies before every send
steps.body: Read the thread just before sending, not only when the list was last updated. Count a reply from anyone at their domain as a reply.

steps.title: Update the list after each email
steps.body: Last contact to today, next follow-up to the next gap, and a note of what you sent.

example.h2: A worked example: a leads app in 50agents
body: In 50agents, one sentence to Captain builds you a leads app on the steps above. It asks where new leads come from and whether follow-ups should go from your email, then builds the list (name, email, phone, company, source, stage, deal size, last contact, next follow-up, notes), a Pipeline board and a Follow up view. Its AI agent, Closer, brings new leads in from the last day’s email each weekday at 9:00, marks a lead Replied when they answer, and drafts a follow-up in the same thread when a Contacted lead has been quiet for 3 days. Every follow-up waits for your yes.

wrong.title: A follow-up after they replied
wrong.body: They answered from a colleague’s address, or started a new thread. Check the thread and their domain right before each send.

wrong.title: An out-of-office stops the sequence
wrong.body: An auto-reply counts as a reply. Treat replies that say "out of office" or "automatic reply" as not replied, and follow up after their return date.

wrong.title: Your whole Gmail stops sending
wrong.body: A big sequence hit the daily limit, which blocks all your mail, not just the automation. Keep automated sends well under it.

wrong.title: Follow-ups at 3 in the morning
wrong.body: The tool ran in another timezone. Set sends for working hours in the lead’s timezone where you know it.

wrong.title: The same email three times
wrong.body: Each follow-up is a copy of the first. Write each one to offer something new, or stop after one.

faqs.q: Does Gmail have automatic follow-ups built in?
faqs.a: No. Gmail’s nudges remind you to follow up; they do not send anything. Sending needs an add-on, a CRM sequence or an automation tool.

faqs.q: How long should I wait before following up with a lead?
faqs.a: Two to three working days for a lead who asked you something, a week for a cold contact. Stop after two or three follow-ups with no reply.

faqs.q: Will automated follow-ups hurt my deliverability?
faqs.a: A few dozen personal follow-ups in the same thread will not. Hundreds of near-identical emails a day from one account can, and they also risk Gmail’s sending limits.
